messages:
tariq: heads-up: during a controlled peering swap in staging a few tenants reported outbound source IP changes mid-TCP session. app telemetry showed retry storms.
sana: thanks, saw the alerts. looks like connector handoff is immediate when the control plane flips which drops conntrack entries.
julian: is the eviction policy TTL-driven? iirc operator nukes the connector record once CP misses heartbeat.
tariq: yes. ttl=60s in staging. when eviction happens we detach the ENI and spin up a new connector -> new IP. flows break.
mei: quick idea: extend connector lifecycle with a short data-plane grace so existing flows keep SNAT mapping until they idle. call it "lease-extension" or "handoff-mode".
sana: how would data-plane signal activity? conntrack local only. relays/proxies complicate visibility.
julian: two options: 1) agent-side keepalive that increments lease if local conntrack>0, capped by a max_grace; 2) dataplane emits periodic flow-heartbeats to control-plane for active connectors.
mei: option 1 is simpler and avoids new RPC paths. agent requests lease_extend(+30s) while active flows exist, up to max 10m. when agent goes quiet, lease expires and normal eviction proceeds.
infra-bot: note: ENI quotas are limited for some accounts. long leases increase IP pressure. add quota check to operator.
sana: to mitigate ENI exhaustion, combine with a "soft-handback" mode: mark connector as evicted in CP but keep it proxying only existing flows for grace window. new flows prefer new connector.
julian: that requires per-connector routing preference. simplified behavior: a) new connector gets BGP/route active b) old connector keeps NAT table for existing 5m c) operator removes old route only after drain.
mei: pseudo-config we discussed in spike:
```
connector_lease_sec: 60
lease_extend_step: 30
max_lease_extension: 600  # 10 min
soft_handoff_window: 300   # 5 min
idle_detection_ms: 120000  # 2 min
```
tariq: we should also have a fallback SNAT lookup: if packet arrives with source and no primary mapping, consult per-tenant fallback map before rewriting. reduces blackholing during races. small lookup cost.
sana: edge case: TLS client IP logging for customers who whitelist our IPs. if IP flips we need to notify them or offer stable IP opt-in per tenant (paid add-on?).
julian: ops runbook additions: 1) how to force immediate eviction (ENI exhausted) 2) how to trigger manual drain for a connector 3) metrics to monitor.
infra-bot: recommended metrics: connector_lease_extensions_total, connector_soft_handoff_seconds, snat_fallback_invocations, tenant_ip_flip_count.
oncall-bot: scheduled test: peering-hand-off-canary on 2026-04-02T03:00Z in canary-account. owners: @mei @tariq.
mei: i'll enable lease-extension flag in canary and add dashboard panels for fallback_invocations & tenant_ip_flip_count.
tariq: i'll run synthetic long-lived flows (tcp upload) and simulate route switch. julian can you prepare rollback steps if ENI pressure spikes?
julian: will do. rollback = disable lease-extend flag + force drain. I'll add automated alert if ENI pool used > 80%.
sana: customer opt-in: add tenant config field stable_ip_opt_in = true/false. doc caveat: may increase cost and reduce scale. support to draft comms.
mei: i opened a short RFC PR with the policy, config knobs, and canary checklist. link shortly.
tariq: perfect. after canary we'll tune defaults (lease step, max) and decide prod rollout. thanks all.
